research_sources.title: Henri Matisse and the cut outs
research_sources.locator: Printed research note M1 in this pack. Based on a museum studio-method account titled Henri Matisse The Cut Outs. Checked 30 October 2026.
facts: Henri Matisse made paintings and drawings. Later, he made art with cut paper.
His helpers painted sheets of paper. He cut shapes from the sheets. He chose where the shapes went.
Pins held the shapes in place. He could try a new layout before fixing them. For large works, he asked helpers to move the shapes.
research_sources.question: How did Matisse test and change a layout?
research_sources.interpretation: Moving shapes might inspire me to try more than one layout. This is my idea about his method, not a claim about his private feelings.

research_sources.title: Alma Thomas and abstract painting
research_sources.locator: Printed research note T1 in this pack. Based on a museum collection biography titled Alma Thomas. Checked 30 October 2026.
facts: Alma Thomas was an art teacher. She made art too. She retired from teaching in 1960. She went on to make more paintings.
Her later art has small marks of bright colour. The marks often form a pattern. Her abstract art uses marks and shapes.
Plants and gardens gave her ideas. Space travel gave her ideas too.
research_sources.question: What changed in her career, and what features appear in her later paintings?
research_sources.interpretation: Her repeated marks might inspire me to vary the gaps in my own piece. This is my personal response, not a copy of a painting.
